title: A background container in command palette
summary: The author narrowed the intermittent extra mica-colored container to Command Palette reloads while Windhawk is running with multiple styling extensions; the symptom often disappears when CmdPal starts with Windhawk stopped.

judgment.rationale: The new author comment supplies a bounded A/B condition that is sufficient for maintainer-side reproduction. The visual failing surface is still unconfirmed, so a code design would be speculative until the host HWND, DWM frame, and rounded card backdrop are compared between control and failing runs.
evidence: The author reports the issue is intermittent and now occurs far apart.
The author identifies Windhawk as the likely condition and lists extensions affecting window borders, taskbar styling, animations, and shell surfaces.
The author states the issue often stops when Command Palette loads while Windhawk is not running.
Current CmdPal code separates a transparent MainWindow host HWND from the visible rounded CmdPalMainControl card and its SystemBackdropElement.
No duplicate issue or linked PowerToys fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the Windhawk-on/off reproduction and capture which HWND or XAML surface receives the unexpected mica/background before selecting a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys-side interaction is plausible, but the failing surface and ownership are not confirmed. Do not expose an implementation approval until the focused reproduction distinguishes host-HWND/DWM styling from duplicate card-backdrop attachment.

issue_context.summary: An intermittent mica-colored background container appears around Command Palette, most likely when Windhawk styling extensions are active; the author reports normal behavior more often when Windhawk is stopped.
known_information: The issue concerns the stable Microsoft Store Command Palette.
The author supplied an A/B condition involving Windhawk running versus stopped.
The author listed 14 active Windhawk extensions, including invisible window borders, taskbar styling, Windows animations, and Start/notification styling.
CmdPal MainWindow intentionally uses a transparent host while CmdPalMainControl owns the rounded visible card and backdrop.
No linked fix PR, duplicate, assignee, or existing fork fix is present.
inferences: Windhawk may intermittently alter the borderless host HWND or DWM frame, but the report does not prove that it is the direct cause.
A duplicate or incorrectly retained SystemBackdropElement target is an alternative PowerToys-side hypothesis.
The correct next step is maintainer-side visual-tree and HWND comparison, not another generic log request.
issue_context.analysis: The report now contains the discriminating external-software condition needed for a focused reproduction. The reproduction should compare host bounds/material, DWM frame attributes, and the card backdrop target with Windhawk stopped and active. Only after that comparison should the workflow choose a PowerToys fix or classify the interaction as external.
initial_investigation: Inspected CmdPal MainWindow and CmdPalMainControl ownership of the transparent host and rounded card backdrop.
Reviewed the recent backdrop/controller history around the host/card separation and fallback lifetime handling.
Searched current issue and PR context for a duplicate or covering fix; none was found.

information_gaps.information: A cropped screenshot showing whether the extra container surrounds the rounded card or is inset within it.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes host-HWND/DWM rendering from a duplicate card/backdrop surface.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Upload a cropped screenshot through the GitHub web UI with sensitive content hidden.

information_gaps.information: Exact PowerToys version/build on which the intermittent behavior occurred.
information_gaps.why_needed: CmdPal backdrop ownership changed recently, so the affected build determines the applicable source path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Copy the version from PowerToys About.

information_gaps.why_needed: DWM mica and border behavior can vary by Windows build.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Run winver and provide the edition/build.

actions.label: Reproduce CmdPal with Windhawk styling

prerequisites: Windhawk installed with the author's listed extensions enabled.
A control run with Windhawk fully stopped.
steps: Start Command Palette with Windhawk stopped and record the visible window shape and material.
Start Windhawk with the listed extensions enabled.
Reload or restart Command Palette repeatedly until the extra mica-colored container appears.
Compare host HWND bounds, DWM frame attributes, and CmdPalMainControl card bounds between control and failing runs.
Record whether the extra surface surrounds the card or is attached inside the card visual tree.
reproduce.expected_result: Only the rounded CmdPal card has the configured backdrop; the surrounding host region remains transparent.
reproduce.actual_to_confirm: An additional mica-colored background/container appears around or behind the card only intermittently with Windhawk active.

actions.note: Read-only maintainer reproduction; no upstream issue, comment, label, dashboard, or fork mutation was performed.
